source: Checked-in turns for key-free mode. Not a capture of a live model call. The SQL is executed locally against whichever pack is installed. HbA1c control comes from the shared definition (hba1c-control.sql).

turns.content: Foo Medical's diabetes dashboard shows HbA1c control (share of type 2 diabetes patients' HbA1c results under 7%) dropping. Find out why, back every claim with SQL, and check the rest of the data for other problems that would distort a dashboard. Data is the local synthetic analytics pack.

REPLAY (no key)

I will measure monthly HbA1c control for type 2 diabetes (SNOMED 44054006) with the shared definition in demos/_shared/data-packs/synthea-analytics/hba1c-control.sql: one row per observation, converted to NGSP percent first (mmol/mol rows: 0.09148 * IFCC + 2.152), controlled means under 7 (strict). The same view also reports the naive rate that applies the threshold to raw values, so a unit change shows up as a sharp drop in the naive rate with a new unit beside it.

queries.sql: select month, n, mmol_rows, controlled_n, control_pct, control_pct_naive from hba1c_control_monthly where month >= '2025-12-01' and month < '2026-06-01' order by month

select date_trunc('month', date)::date as month, units, count(*) as n, round(avg(value_num), 1) as avg_value from observations where code = '4548-4' and date >= '2025-12-01' and date < '2026-06-01' group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2
select min(date)::date as start_date, count(*) as n from observations where code = '4548-4' and units = 'mmol/mol'
select distinct e.organization as organization_id from observations o join encounters e on e.id = o.encounter where o.code = '4548-4' and o.units = 'mmol/mol' order by 1
